review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its definitions against Mathlib. The file defines poissonSpectralKernel, normalizedPoissonKernel, conjugatePoissonSpectralKernel, cotlarShiftedSpectralAction and cotlarHilbertSpectralAction. It also uses cotlarPoissonKernel, cotlarConjugatePoissonKernel and cotlarConjugatePoissonAction, which come from HilbertMaximalWeakOneOne, and ordinaryHilbertMultiplier from HilbertL2Fourier. A Mathlib search for "Poisson" found only the Poisson distribution, Poisson summation, and the disc/half-plane Poisson integral in Analysis/Complex/Poisson.lean and Analysis/Complex/Harmonic/Poisson.lean. None of these is the upper half-plane Poisson kernel r/(t²+r²) on ℝ or its Fourier multiplier exp(-2π r |ξ|), so I found no competing Mathlib concept. normalizedPoissonKernel is only a ℂ-valued, 1/π-scaled wrapper that gives a name to an expression already used in fourier_poissonSpectralKernel, so it is not a competing concept. The file uses Real.sign, Real.fourierChar, 𝓕 and 𝓕⁻ from Mathlib. fourier_comp_add_right_real is a theorem rather than a definition, and it specialises Mathlib's VectorFourier.fourierIntegral_comp_add_right, so it falls under the excluded standalone-theorem duplication. Remaining uncertainty is small: I did not check every use of the definitions across the repository.
